mn98:5.1: Then the young brahman Vāseṭṭha said to the young brahman Bhāradvāja,
mn98:5.2: “Bhāradvāja, this Gotama the contemplative—a son of the Sakyans, gone forth from the Sakyan clan—is staying at Icchānaṅgala in the Icchānaṅgala forest grove.
mn98:5.3: And of that Master Gotama this fine reputation has spread:
mn98:5.4: ‘He is indeed a Blessed One, worthy & rightly self-awakened, consummate in clear-knowing & conduct, well-gone, an expert with regard to the cosmos, unexcelled trainer of people fit to be tamed, teacher of devas & human beings, awakened, blessed.’
mn98:5.5: Come, let’s go to Gotama the contemplative and, on arrival, ask him about this matter.
mn98:5.6: However he answers, that’s how we’ll hold it.”
mn98:5.7: “As you say, master,” the young brahman Bhāradvāja responded to the young brahman Vāseṭṭha.

mn98:14.1: When this was said, the young brahmans Vāseṭṭha & Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One:
mn98:14.3: Just as if he were to place upright what was overturned, to reveal what was hidden, to show the way to one who was lost, or to carry a lamp into the dark so that those with eyes could see forms, in the same way has Master Gotama—through many lines of reasoning—made the Dhamma clear.
mn98:14.4: We go to Master Gotama for refuge, to the Dhamma, & to the Saṅgha of monks.
mn98:14.5: May Master Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge from this day forward, for life.”
